headline: Public hearing and scheduled vote on changes to the Debt Management Policy, including related sections of Chapter 2 and Chapter 14 of the City Code.
summary: A public hearing will be held on proposed changes to the Debt Management Policy, and action to endorse them may follow. Changes to Chapter 2 and Chapter 14 of the City Code would need City Council approval, and Chapter 14 changes would also need Planning Board approval.

 PUBLIC COMMENT INFORMATION  
     
  
 
To submit written public comment on an agenda item for which public comment is 
being accepted, email finance@portlandmaine.gov. Submissions must be received by 
12:00 pm the day before the Finance Committee meeting to guarantee their inclusion 
in the agenda packet. All submissions must include the commenter's name and legal 
address. To help ensure your comment is submitted for the correct item, please 
include the name of the agenda item (see below). 
 
 ZOOM MEETING INFORMATION  
     
  
 
This meeting will take place remotely using Zoom. This meeting will be held 
remotely pursuant to the Remote Meeting Policy adopted by the Portland City 
Council. Allow your computer to install the free Zoom app to get the best meeting 
experience. If you are not able to attend live, a recording will be available in the 
Agenda Center following the meeting. For agenda items where public comment is 
scheduled, you will need to use the "raise your hand" feature. To raise your hand via 
the telephone, please hit *9. You will be unmuted by the host when it is time for 
public comment.

 1. Introductions  
     
 2. Finance Policies Updates - Debt Management (Public Hearing and Scheduled Vote)  
     
  
 
At prior meetings, staff discussed concepts for changes to the Debt Management Policy for 
Finance Committee to review and approve. These included elimination of language specific to
2 
the City’s pension obligation bonds (which matured on June 1, 2026), addition of new best 
practices per the latest guidance from credit rating agencies, and work to align internal policy 
with Chapter 2 and Chapter 14 of the City Code.  At the current meeting, staff will discuss next 
steps for approvals including presentation of a clean copy of the Debt Management Policy and 
red lined drafts of applicable sections of Chapter 2 and Chapter 14.  The changes to Chapter 2 
and Chapter 14 will require City Council approval and the changes to Chapter 14 will also 
require Planning Board approval.  The Committee will hold a public hearing and consider 
taking action to endorse the changes.
